description.summary: the desktop shell's surface roles and system events

protocol.description:
The desktop shell tells the compositor which of its surfaces is the bar, the dock, the switcher and so on, and the compositor tells the shell about the events only it can see: the real modifier keys, modifier gestures, the app switcher, Mission Control's layout, hot corners, edge reveals and the kill chord.
Apps are named by their app key string and windows by their ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier string, because the shell binds this global on a different connection from the one that holds its toplevel handles, and no Wayland object crosses connections.
This protocol is a draft. Until it is declared stable, version 1 may change in place with every client and the server updated together. Version 2 adds, without touching version 1's messages or opcodes, which outputs Mission Control is open on, Space pictures and dropping a window on a Space in Mission Control; every message it adds says `since="2"`. Version 3 adds, again after everything older, a "new desktop" drop target: dropping a window on it makes a Space with the window; every message it adds says `since="3"`. Version 4 adds, again after everything older, the start and the end of a window drag in Mission Control; every message it adds says `since="4"`. Version 5 adds, again after everything older, the compositor asking the shell to ask the person whether a program may use one of seven powers (see the screen, type and click, help with typing, read the clipboard, lock the screen, change displays, manage windows); every message it adds says `since="5"`. A shell that bound an older version never receives the version 5 events and has nothing to answer; a program that needs asking is then refused, without being remembered. Version 6 adds, again after everything older, the compositor asking the shell whether the person keeps a display setup a program changed (with a time limit, after which the old setup returns), and the error `answered_too_soon` for an answer that comes before the question could have been read; every message and entry it adds says `since="6"`. A shell that bound an older version is never asked, and the change is reverted when the time runs out. Version 7 adds, again after everything older, the shell choosing whether the bar stays up in full screen, the shell telling the compositor how much motion the person allows, and `reveal_on_output`, which names the output an edge reveal happened on; every message and entry it adds says `since="7"`. A shell that bound version 7 receives `reveal_on_output` in place of `reveal`; one that bound an older version receives `reveal` as before, gets the reveal in every full screen, and gets full motion.

request.name: set_role

description.summary: give a shell surface its role

request.description: `surface` must be a layer surface of this client; anything else raises `bad_surface`. A role held by another live surface raises `role_taken`, except that `bar` and `dock` are held once per output: each output has its own bar and its own dock (the output the layer surface was made for, or the one the compositor put it on), and only a second bar or dock on the same output raises `role_taken`.

request.name: set_minimise_target

description.summary: where a window minimises to

request.description: The rectangle, local to the dock surface, that the window named by `toplevel` shrinks into when minimised. Replaces an earlier target for that window.

description.summary: forget a window's minimise target

request.description: Answers `window_menu`. An unknown window or entry is ignored; so is an entry the window's state does not offer.

request.name: split_pick

description.summary: the person picked the other half of a Split View

request.description: Answers `split_choose`: `toplevel` is one of the candidates sent after it. A window that is no candidate now, or no choosing, is ignored.

request.name: split_cancel

description.summary: the person turned the choice of a Split View down

request.description: Escape, or a click elsewhere. The first window stays alone, full screen. Without a choosing it is ignored.

request.name: split_divide

description.summary: the divider of a Split View was moved

request.description: `toplevel` is either window of the pair. `share` is the leading (left) window's part of the width, in thousandths; the compositor keeps it between 200 and 800 and holds each half to its window's smallest width. A window that is in no Split View is ignored.

event.name: window_menu

description.summary: show a window's menu

event.description: The pointer rested on the window's green light, or the window asked for its menu. The shell draws the menu at (`x`, `y`), in global logical pixels, with the entries of `window_entry` in menu order. Bit `n` of `enabled` is set when the entry with code `n` can be picked now; the others are shown dimmed. A pick comes back as `window_menu_pick`; a dismissal sends nothing.

event.name: split_choose

description.summary: offer the other half of a Split View

event.description: `first` went full screen on `side`. The shell offers the windows named by the `split_candidate` events that follow at once, most recently used first, for the other half. The offer lasts until `split_choice_end`; the answer is `split_pick` or `split_cancel`.

event.name: split_candidate

description.summary: a window that can fill the other half

event.description: One per candidate, straight after `split_choose`.

event.name: split_choice_end

description.summary: the choice of a Split View is over

event.description: A pick, a cancel, or `first` left full screen or closed: the shell takes its offer away.

event.name: killed

description.summary: the kill chord was pressed

event.description: Every agent lease has ended.

request.name: get_space_capture_source

description.summary: a picture source for one Space of an output

request.description: Creates an ext_image_capture_source_v1 that shows the Space `space_id` of `output`: its windows where they sit on the output, over a transparent background (the shell draws the wallpaper), scaled to `width` by `height` pixels (the shell's miniature; each side is kept between 1 and 1024). Use it with the standard ext_image_copy_capture_manager_v1; the session's buffer constraints announce that size, and a frame is sent only when something in the Space changed since the last one. The windows are drawn without their frames. A Space that does not exist, or is not on `output`, gives a source whose sessions are stopped at once; so does a Space that is removed while the session lives. Version 2 drew only the Space the output shows now. From version 3 any desktop Space of the output has a picture: the windows of a Space that is not shown are laid out where they would sit if it were shown, for the picture only, and the picture is sent again when one of them changes. A full-screen or Split View Space shows its windows as they sit.

request.name: space_target_clear

description.summary: forget the Space targets of an output

request.description: Removes every rectangle set with `space_target` for `output`. Send it, then the new rectangles, when the shell's Spaces bar changes.

request.name: space_target

description.summary: a place a window can be dropped on a Space

request.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control, releasing it over this rectangle moves it to the Space `space_id`. The rectangle is in global logical pixels (like `overview_space`). Later targets are in front of earlier ones. An empty rectangle raises `bad_target`. A Space that does not exist is kept but never hit.

request.name: space_target_new

description.summary: the place a window can be dropped to make a new Space

request.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control, releasing it over this rectangle (the Spaces bar's "add desktop" tile) makes a new Space on `output` and moves the window to it; Mission Control stays open. The rectangle is in global logical pixels, like `space_target`; it is in front of every `space_target` rectangle of the output and there is one per output, a later request replaces it. An empty rectangle removes it (no error). `space_target_clear` leaves it alone.

request.name: permission_answer

description.summary: the person answered a question from permission_ask

request.description:
`ask` is the id from `permission_ask`. The first answer to an ask settles it; an answer for an ask that is unknown, already answered or withdrawn is ignored, so a late answer does no harm.
`allow` lets the program use the power: what it was waiting for goes ahead, and the requests the compositor held meanwhile are replayed in order (up to a fixed limit; the compositor says in its own documentation which are held). When `memory` was `remembered` the allow is kept; when it was `this_time_only` it lasts while the program stays connected and is never written down (Allow Once).
`deny` and `dismissed` both refuse the power, and the program gets the refusal its own protocol has (a capture stops, a clipboard source is finished, a lock is refused, a change to the displays fails, a window list ends). They differ in what is kept: `deny` is kept when `memory` was `remembered`, and the program is not asked again until the person changes it in Settings; `dismissed` is never kept and the program may be asked again after a while.
The shell answers each ask it showed once, and answers `dismissed` when its sheet goes away without an answer.

request.name: displays_trial_answer

description.summary: the person answered a question from displays_trial

request.description:
`trial` is the id from `displays_trial`. The first answer settles it; an answer for a trial that is unknown, over or withdrawn is ignored (it is not an error), so a late answer does no harm. `keep` makes the new setup the one the displays have; `revert` puts the previous one back at once. Escape, or the sheet going away, answers `revert`.
An answer that comes less than half a second after the event is the error `answered_too_soon`, as for `permission_answer`.

event.name: overview_output

description.summary: Mission Control is open or closed on an output

event.description: Sent for every output, just before each `overview_state`, and for an output that is plugged in while Mission Control is open. Mission Control follows the Mac's way with separate Spaces on each display: it opens on every output at once, each with its own windows and its own Spaces bar. `shown` is `shown` for an output whose Mission Control is up (entering, open or leaving) and `hidden` when it is closed. The shell draws its Spaces bar on the outputs that are shown only.

event.name: drop_target

description.summary: the dragged window is over a Space target

event.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control (a press on its slot, then a move past a small distance), the Space target under the pointer changed. `space_id` is the Space of the `space_target` rectangle under the pointer on `output`, or null when none is: the shell highlights it. It is sent with null when the drag ends, by a drop or by the window flying back.

event.name: drop_target_new

description.summary: the dragged window is over the new-Space target

event.description: While a window is dragged in Mission Control, the pointer entered (`shown`) or left (`hidden`) the `space_target_new` rectangle of `output`: the shell highlights the "add desktop" tile. It is sent `hidden` when the drag ends, by a drop or by the window flying back. `drop_target` is sent null for the same output when this one is `shown`.

event.name: window_drag_begin

description.summary: a window drag started in Mission Control

event.description: A press on a window's slot moved past the small distance, so the window is being dragged on `output`: the shell shows which targets (the Spaces of its bar and the "add desktop" tile) accept it. `drop_target` and `drop_target_new` follow while the pointer moves. One drag at a time; it ends with `window_drag_end`.

event.name: window_drag_end

description.summary: the window drag in Mission Control is over

event.description: The window was released or the drag was abandoned. `outcome` says where it went. It comes after the `drop_target` and `drop_target_new` messages that clear the highlight.

event.name: permission_ask

description.summary: ask the person whether a program may use a power

event.description:
A program used `power` for the first time and the compositor does not already know the answer. The shell puts a question on screen that names the program (a desktop entry or app id found from `subject`, else the file name), says what the power lets it do, and offers Allow and Don't Allow. When `memory` is `this_time_only` the first button is Allow Once, and the sheet says the program cannot be recognised so it will be asked again. Escape, or the sheet going away, answers `dismissed`. The words are the shell's.
`subject` is at most 4096 bytes. The same program using the same power again while an ask is open joins that ask. The compositor keeps at most one ask open toward the shell and sends the next one after the answer or `permission_withdraw`; a shell should still be ready to show several, one after another.
Replay: an ask stays open until it is answered or withdrawn, whether or not a shell is connected. When a shell binds this global (it starts after the compositor, or it restarted), the compositor sends every open ask again, in the order they were first sent and with the same `ask` ids, straight after the other events of the bind; a shell that restarted while its sheet was up sees the question again. An ask also stays open after the program that raised it has gone, so that the answer counts the next time the program runs; it is withdrawn when its time runs out.
Denial: with no shell bound, the compositor waits for a short time after it started, then refuses the program without remembering anything. It also refuses without remembering, and sends no ask, while the screen is locked and when too many asks are already waiting. An ask nobody answers in time is withdrawn and the program is refused, not remembered. A shell that bound a version older than 5 never sees any of this, and the program is refused the same way.
`ask` is unique among the asks of one compositor run and is not reused.

arg.name: ask
arg.summary: the ask's id; the answer and the withdrawal name it

arg.name: subject
arg.summary: the program's path or the sandboxed app's id, at most 4096 bytes

event.name: permission_withdraw

description.summary: the question is no longer needed

event.description: The compositor no longer needs the answer to `ask`: it timed out, the screen was locked, the person already settled it in Settings, the administrator's rule decided it, or the program that raised it is gone and its time ran out. The shell takes the sheet down without answering, and a late `permission_answer` for it is ignored. Nothing is remembered because of a withdrawal. An unknown `ask` is ignored.

event.name: displays_trial

description.summary: ask the person whether to keep a changed display setup

event.description:
A program other than the shell changed the displays (size, scale, position, or turned one on or off). The compositor has applied the change and goes back to the previous setup after `seconds` unless the person keeps it: no answer within that time reverts. The shell puts "Keep these display settings?" on screen with Keep and Revert and a countdown of `seconds`. The words are the shell's.
At most one trial is open. A further change by a program while it is open restarts the time and sends this event again with the full `seconds`; the shell restarts its countdown (the `trial` id may stay the same, so a shell treats an id it already shows as the same question). A shell that bound a version older than 6 is never asked, and the change is reverted when the time runs out.
A shell that binds while a trial is open (it restarted) is sent this event at once, with `seconds` set to the time left, so the question survives the shell's restart the way `permission_ask` does.

arg.name: trial
arg.summary: the trial's id; the answer and the end name it

event.name: displays_trial_end

description.summary: the question is over

event.description: The shell takes the question down without answering. It is sent when the trial was answered (by any shell connection), when the time ran out and the change was reverted, when the shell itself changed the displays, and when a newer trial replaced this one. An answer for an ended or unknown trial is ignored.

description.summary: what the bar does in full screen

entry.name: reveal
entry.summary: hidden; it slides in when the pointer rests at the top edge

entry.name: keep
entry.summary: it stays up and the full-screen window is sized below it

description.summary: how much motion the person allows

entry.name: full
entry.summary: slides and zooms

entry.name: reduced
entry.summary: cross-fades in place of slides

request.name: set_full_screen_bar

description.summary: choose what the bar does in full screen

request.description: With `reveal` (the start state) the bar is behind a full-screen window and slides in over it when the pointer rests at the top edge, as `reveal_on_output` tells. With `keep` the bar stays up on every output and a full-screen window is sized to the output less the bar's exclusive zone; no top-edge reveal happens. The dock still reveals at the bottom edge either way. It applies to every output and to full-screen windows already shown (they are configured again). The shell sends it after binding and whenever the person changes the setting; the last one wins.

request.name: set_motion

description.summary: say how much motion the person allows

request.description: With `reduced`, the compositor's own moves that have a quieter form use it: the bar and the dock cross-fade in place of sliding in full screen. The start state is `full`. The shell sends it after binding and whenever the person changes the setting; the last one wins.

event.name: reveal_on_output

description.summary: an edge reveal changed on an output

event.description: In full screen on `output`, the bar or the dock of that output slides in from its edge (`shown`, sent as the slide in starts), or has slid away (`hidden`, sent when the slide away has ended, or at once when the full screen ends). Sent in place of `reveal` to a shell that bound version 7.
